sources.title: Fundamental Information Analysis
sources.mechanism_summary: Fundamental operating and accounting signals can contain incremental information related to earnings persistence and value relevance.
sources.claim_boundary: Selected signal information content does not establish a universal causal driver ontology or invariant forecasting performance.

sources.title: Fundamental Analysis, Future Earnings, and Stock Prices
sources.mechanism_summary: Fundamental signals are empirically related to future earnings changes and analyst forecast revisions, with contextual conditioning affecting information content.
sources.claim_boundary: Predictive association is not causal identification and signal usefulness is context dependent.

sources.title: Ratio Analysis and Equity Valuation: From Research to Practice
sources.mechanism_summary: Financial analysis can be hierarchical, separating operating and financing activities and treating lower-level ratios as finer information for higher-level future payoff ratios.
sources.claim_boundary: Analytical hierarchy is a decomposition and forecasting scaffold, not causal proof or a universal sector ontology.

sources.title: Accounting Earnings and Cash Flows as Measures of Firm Performance: The Role of Accounting Accruals
sources.mechanism_summary: Accruals can improve performance measurement when raw cash flows suffer timing and matching problems.
sources.claim_boundary: Cash flow is not automatically economically superior to earnings; divergence needs timing, working-capital and investment context.

sources.title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?
sources.mechanism_summary: Accrual and cash-flow components contain different information about future earnings persistence in the studied sample.
sources.claim_boundary: The result is not a fraud diagnostic and does not imply all accruals are low quality or a live trading rule.

sources.title: The Quality of Accruals and Earnings: The Role of Accrual Estimation Errors
sources.mechanism_summary: Working-capital accrual quality decreases with estimation error because accruals shift cash-flow recognition across periods.
sources.claim_boundary: This is one dimension of earnings quality, not a complete quality or misconduct score.

sources.title: Accrual Reliability, Earnings Persistence and Stock Prices
sources.mechanism_summary: Less reliable accrual categories are associated with lower earnings persistence.
sources.claim_boundary: Reliability classification does not prove manipulation and historical mispricing evidence is not a universal live strategy.

sources.title: Accrued Earnings and Growth: Implications for Future Profitability and Market Mispricing
sources.mechanism_summary: Some accrual effects can be interpreted as part of a broader growth-in-net-operating-assets and diminishing-returns mechanism.
sources.claim_boundary: Normal investment and growth must be separated from accounting deterioration.

sources.title: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows
sources.mechanism_summary: IAS 7 defines operating, investing and financing cash-flow presentation and reconciliation requirements.
sources.claim_boundary: Normative reporting authority is not predictive theory or asset-pricing evidence and is excluded from Shadow TheoryObjects.

sources.title: Agency Costs, Net Worth, and Business Fluctuations
sources.mechanism_summary: Higher borrower net worth lowers external-finance agency costs, affecting investment and amplifying business fluctuations.
sources.claim_boundary: The model identifies a balance-sheet mechanism; it does not imply every aggregate credit change causes asset-price moves.

sources.title: Credit Cycles
sources.mechanism_summary: Collateral values, borrowing limits and asset prices interact dynamically, allowing shocks to persist and amplify across sectors.
sources.claim_boundary: Collateral-feedback theory requires observable borrower/collateral structure and cannot be inferred from credit correlation alone.

sources.title: Credit Booms Gone Bust: Monetary Policy, Leverage Cycles, and Financial Crises, 1870-2008
sources.mechanism_summary: Long-run cross-country evidence shows credit growth is a powerful predictor of financial crises and provides replication materials.
sources.claim_boundary: Predictive historical association does not by itself identify the micro causal channel or imply deterministic crisis timing.

sources.title: When Credit Bites Back
sources.journal_or_authority: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 45(s2):3-28
sources.mechanism_summary: Across 14 advanced countries, more credit-intensive expansions tend to be followed by deeper recessions and slower recoveries.
sources.claim_boundary: Local-projection historical evidence supports macro financial amplification but does not establish borrower-specific causal transmission without sectoral evidence.

sources.title: Capital Asset Prices: A Theory of Market Equilibrium under Conditions of Risk
sources.mechanism_summary: The model distinguishes a pure time price from compensation for non-diversifiable risk under restrictive equilibrium assumptions.
sources.claim_boundary: CAPM assumptions are restrictive and the model is not a universal target-price engine or universal discount-rate estimator.

sources.title: The Dividend-Price Ratio and Expectations of Future Dividends and Discount Factors
sources.mechanism_summary: A log-linear present-value relation connects dividend-price ratios to expected future dividend growth, discount rates and unexplained components.
sources.claim_boundary: The decomposition is an expectations accounting identity/model framework, not an automatic forecast or market-timing oracle.

sources.title: Presidential Address: Discount Rates
sources.mechanism_summary: Discount-rate variation is a central organizing issue in modern asset pricing and affects time-series and cross-sectional return interpretation.
sources.claim_boundary: A synthesis of discount-rate variation does not grant stable forecasting authority to any single predictor or imply one universal required-return measure.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Look at The Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
sources.mechanism_summary: Many proposed equity-premium predictors performed poorly and unstably out of sample relative to simple historical-mean benchmarks.
sources.claim_boundary: Interpretive decompositions must not self-promote into predictive market-timing authority without independent PIT/OOS evidence.

sources.title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
sources.mechanism_summary: A dynamic market-microstructure model formalizes market depth and price impact as dimensions of liquidity and information incorporation.
sources.claim_boundary: Model depth is not the same as realized stress exit capacity across all market structures or funding states.

sources.title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
sources.mechanism_summary: A simple absolute-return-to-dollar-volume proxy captures an illiquidity dimension associated with expected and contemporaneous stock returns.
sources.claim_boundary: Liquidity is multidimensional; the Amihud measure alone cannot establish executable stress-exit capacity.

sources.title: Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns
sources.mechanism_summary: Expected returns are related to sensitivity to aggregate liquidity fluctuations, separating liquidity risk from a security's own static trading condition.
sources.claim_boundary: Historical liquidity-risk pricing does not by itself specify a live liquidation horizon, slippage or funding constraint.

sources.title: Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity
sources.mechanism_summary: Market liquidity and trader funding liquidity can reinforce each other, producing liquidity spirals and abrupt deterioration under stress.
sources.claim_boundary: The model motivates stress-state interaction but requires observable funding/margin conditions and does not imply ADV is sufficient.

sources.title: Determinants of Portfolio Performance
sources.mechanism_summary: Portfolio returns can be compared with a policy benchmark to attribute performance to policy, market timing and security selection activities.
sources.claim_boundary: The framework answers a portfolio attribution question and does not by itself identify causal economic drivers of every realized return.

sources.title: Does Asset Allocation Policy Explain 40, 90, or 100 Percent of Performance?
sources.mechanism_summary: The apparent importance of asset-allocation policy changes materially depending on whether the question concerns time-series variability, cross-fund variation, or return level.
sources.claim_boundary: Attribution conclusions are question-dependent; an R-squared about variability must not be relabeled as percentage of return causally created by policy.

sources.title: A Variance Decomposition for Stock Returns
sources.mechanism_summary: Unexpected stock returns can be decomposed into revisions in expected future dividends and expected future returns using a VAR-based present-value framework.
sources.claim_boundary: Return-news decomposition is model-based and does not automatically identify the unique real-world causal event behind a realized return.

sources.title: Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds
sources.mechanism_summary: Common stock and bond return factors explain shared variation and provide a basis for separating systematic factor exposure from residual return.
sources.claim_boundary: Factor exposure is statistical attribution and not proof that a factor causally generated a specific realized P&L path.
